_conclusion: A floor is a spread statistic estimated from nine paired repeats and carries large uncertainty; an achieved fraction is a median and is robust. So whether a submission RESOLVES can depend on which session its validator calibrated in, and `burnish calibrate --merge` folds sessions together keeping the worst floor per cell.
_floor_method: Two arms, both the unmodified base, interleaved with every guard a scored comparison uses. The floor is the larger of the paired control-vs-control spread and the instrument's own resolution.
_floor_stability: A floor is a spread statistic and is not stable between sessions: measured twice on one RTX 5090, hours apart, the per-cell floors here moved by up to 24x while the achieved fractions held to three significant figures. That is expected -- a median is robust and a spread over nine repeats is not -- but it means whether a submission RESOLVES can depend on which session the box was calibrated in. `--merge` folds sessions together keeping the worst floor per cell, which can only refuse a gain too small to see rather than credit noise as a contribution.
_what_this_is: The raw first calibration session of the same physical card as eval/cells/BG-1/reference.json, taken with the same driver and the same build (the vendor kernels as `cuda`), eleven minutes before the session it was merged into. It is not the calibration anything is scored against -- reference.json is -- and it is kept because it is the evidence for what docs/EVAL.md and docs/STATUS.md say about how floors move between sessions.
_why_it_is_committed: Those documents state that per-cell noise floors move by up to 24x between sessions while achieved fractions hold to three significant figures. That is a measured claim, and for a while the only place its numbers existed in this repository was a test docstring -- which is prose. A published figure whose measurement is not in the tree cannot be checked by anybody, which is the one thing this repository is built not to do.

device_probe._clocks_note: Clocks are not pinned and cannot be in a container. Only paired interleaved same-box deltas mean anything; absolute times from two different sessions are not comparable.
